title: Computerized System Validation (CSV) & GAMP 5 Nomenclature
description: Navigate GAMP 5 terminology, V-Model qualification stages (URS, FRS, DQ, IQ, OQ, PQ), and traceability matrix nomenclature in pharmaceutical engineering.
learning_objectives: Distinguish correctly between Installation Qualification (IQ), Operational Qualification (OQ), and Performance Qualification (PQ)
Identify GAMP 5 software categories (Category 1, 3, 4, 5) and associated testing rigor
Articulate CSV discrepancies and CAPAs using standard international industry terms

questions.prompt: A User Requirements Specification (URS) defines what the system _____ do from the end-user's operational perspective.

explanations.correct: 'must' precisely expresses mandatory functional requirements in a pharmaceutical URS.

questions.cz_learning_point: In validation engineering, a URS outlines what the system 'must' achieve, avoiding ambiguous colloquialisms.

questions.prompt: During _____ Qualification, engineers verify that wiring, piping, power supply, and physical components match engineering schematics.

explanations.correct: Installation Qualification (IQ) verifies physical installation against manufacturer drawings.
explanations.wrong_A: PQ verifies consistent batch output under production conditions.
explanations.wrong_B: OQ tests operating limits and alarm thresholds.
explanations.wrong_D: DQ verifies that design meets URS requirements before construction.

questions.cz_learning_point: IQ (Installation Qualification) = instalace a zapojení dle specifikace. Do not confuse with OQ (funkční zkoušky) or PQ (výrobní výkonnost).

questions.prompt: Under GAMP 5 classification, off-the-shelf non-configured software such as firmware or standard operating systems is Category _____.

explanations.correct: GAMP Category 1 covers Infrastructure Software (OS, databases, network firmware).
explanations.wrong_B: Category 3 is non-configured software products (run-as-is applications).
explanations.wrong_C: Category 4 is configured software products (SCADA, MES, LIMS).

questions.cz_learning_point: GAMP 5 Category 1 = Infrastructure software. Category 3 = Non-configured COTS, Category 4 = Configured, Category 5 = Custom code.

questions.prompt: The document mapping every single user requirement forward to functional design, test scripts, and test results is the _____.

explanations.correct: The Traceability Matrix (TM) ensures end-to-end verification of all URS requirements in test scripts.
explanations.wrong_C: Site Master File describes overall facility GMP operations.

questions.cz_learning_point: Traceability Matrix (matice sledovatelnosti požadavků) links each URS item directly to corresponding IQ/OQ/PQ protocols.

questions.prompt: Testing the sterile filling line with placebo media across worst-case processing limits belongs to _____ Qualification.

explanations.correct: Performance Qualification (PQ) evaluates overall process effectiveness and sterile capability using simulated media/placebo.
explanations.wrong_D: Maintenance is routine servicing, not a qualification stage.

questions.cz_learning_point: PQ (Performance Qualification) evaluates the integrated process under simulated or actual production conditions.

questions.prompt: In CSV discrepancy reporting, when an actual test result fails to meet the pre-approved acceptance criteria, engineers raise a _____.

explanations.correct: A 'deviation' (or test incident) is the formal GMP term for an outcome that departs from approved protocols.
explanations.wrong_A: 'waiver' is a formal relinquishment of a requirement.
explanations.wrong_C: 'concession' is an agreement to accept non-conforming product.
explanations.wrong_D: 'permission' is a general word, not GMP terminology.

questions.cz_learning_point: In GAMP 5 and GMP validation, an unexpected test failure is recorded as a 'deviation' (odchylka) or 'test incident'.

questions.prompt: GAMP Category 5 represents _____ software, requiring full lifecycle testing, rigorous code reviews, and comprehensive architecture audit.

explanations.correct: Category 5 applies to custom (bespoke) software developed specifically for the application.

questions.cz_learning_point: GAMP 5: Category 4 is 'Configured' (SCADA/LIMS templates), while Category 5 is 'Custom' (zakázkový kód).

questions.prompt: Operational Qualification (OQ) tests must confirm that all critical safety alarms and interlocks _____ within specified limits.

explanations.correct: Plural subject 'alarms and interlocks' takes base verb 'operate' following 'confirm that'.
explanations.wrong_B: Participle alone cannot act as predicate.
explanations.wrong_C: Infinitive with 'to' cannot serve as finite verb in that-clause.
explanations.wrong_D: Present continuous is less appropriate for specifying functional qualification criteria.

questions.cz_learning_point: OQ protocols test that equipment modules 'operate' reliably across operating ranges.

questions.prompt: The regulatory acronym CAPA stands for Corrective and _____ Actions.

explanations.correct: CAPA = Corrective and Preventive Actions (nápravná a preventivní opatření).

questions.cz_learning_point: CAPA stands for 'Corrective and Preventive Actions' (preventivní, nikoliv *protective* ani *predictive*).

questions.prompt: When an operator modifies an electronic setpoint, 21 CFR Part 11 requires that the system log the user ID, timestamp, and _____.

explanations.correct: Part 11 audit trails require recording the who, when, what, and 'reason for change'.
explanations.wrong_A: Salary level is irrelevant to GMP audit trails.
explanations.wrong_C: Printer model is not an audit trail requirement.
explanations.wrong_D: Shift duration is not part of record change logging.

questions.cz_learning_point: Under 21 CFR Part 11, audit trails must capture: identity of user, timestamp, previous value, new value, and 'reason for change'.
